Latest Update: Harry Kane injury could force Bayern Munich into £44m transfer dilemma amid Arsenal, Man United interest

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39.
  • Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.
  • The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39.

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially crucial difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a new long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own prepares have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

There remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the new recruits to settle.

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It notes much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make big improvements, there’s no question about it,’ mentioned the manager.

According to recent reports, ‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

In a recent development, ‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty quickly.’.

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several massive-hitters to come in without delay in the New Year.

‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

According to recent reports, ‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

In a recent development, ‘Domestic football is really important to the football club, of course,’ he stated. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

Sources indicate that ‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

It has been revealed that ‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

It has been revealed that the form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

Industry observers note that ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

In a recent development, ‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.

Sources indicate that fondazione Milan will be the Match Charity Partner for AC Milan vs. Frosinone on Sunday, and Matteo Gabbia has spoken as part of the initiative.

Sources indicate that since 2003, the Foundation has used sport as a tool for change, reaching more than 200,000 young people through 288 projects in Italy and 25 other countries. More than €13m has been invested over the years on various projects to help those that are less fortunate.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, before kick-off on Sunday, the beneficiaries of the various schemes will take a photo with the starting lineup. They will also take part in pitch-side activities alongside Massimo Ambrosini, Daniele Massaro and Matteo Gabbia, who recently visited the Calcio Seduto project. Gabbia spoke at the event.

According to recent reports, “It’s not easy to sum up in just a few minutes what Franco (Baresi) was like as a person and as a player. He was a key figure for the entire AC Milan club, for us kids who are trying to live up to him, and above all for all those people who always told me about his games.

“It’s always exciting for me to hear people talk about Franco and what he achieved with these colours, as a player and as a man.

Sources indicate that “I think Franco is a legend. Fondazione Milan embodies all the beauty and importance that Baresi had. I was moved when I met and got to know the kids from the sitting football team last week.

“I’m sure that if Franco had been there, he would have been proud of everything he organized and created for this foundation.”.

A post shared by Fondazione Milan (@fondazionemilan).

“I’m feeling better. It was a strange start to the season, and I was a bit disappointed personally. Hopefully, from the moment I return, it can be a positive season for me too.”.

According to recent reports, the pregame will also honour the memory of Franco Baresi and his bond with Fondazione Milan. He was a dedicated supporter of its projects, including as a member of its Board of Directors. Club employees will take part in the tribute, along with his longtime teammate and friend Daniele Massaro.

At Sunday’s match, fans can continue to support the Foundation’s projects through donations and auctions of players’ shirts, helping create fresh opportunities for other young people.

Several clubs, including Aston Villa, are said to hold an interest in negotiating a deal with United's hierarchy.

Amad's representatives are also allegedly of the opinion that a move away from Man United may suit the player.

Nevertheless, at a time when a proven world-class forward is being linked with a transfer to the Premier League giants, United chiefs remain in control of Amad's future.

Amad has contributed a respectable 16 goals and 17 assists from his 105 appearances since his arrival at United in 2021.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.
  • The company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September.
  • The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

The company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives mentioned the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

According to recent reports, "The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz mentioned in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

Here are some of the key Q3 figures:.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing looks to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

CEO Oliver Blume plans to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the plan, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz stated the figures revealed the urgency underlying these aims, saying the company needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz said the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he noted.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00.
  • Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.
  • The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00.

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

In a recent development, guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Industry observers note that guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

"I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them.".

Recent findings suggest that almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us.".

According to recent reports, guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, New York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

In a recent development, his journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

Recent findings suggest that the visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

Industry observers note that for Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

According to recent reports, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

Industry observers note that the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

Industry observers note that “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman mentioned. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

It has been revealed that “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Industry observers note that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Recent findings suggest that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

Sources indicate that england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Recent findings suggest that tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the initiative and being patient.”.

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

It has been revealed that “My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

In a recent development, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman remarked. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

According to recent reports, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

According to recent reports, toone swiftly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 11:18, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:35.

Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.

The Citizens are seeking to bounce back from a run of three successive top-flight defeats, most recently losing 3-1 away against Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Manager Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to the side that were beaten at the City Ground, with Fernandez, Cherki and Josko Gvardiol all dropping down to the substitutes’ bench.

While Cherki scored in the defeat to Forest, Gvardiol was at fault for a first-half goal conceded by City and Fernandez’s position in midfield has come under question in recent weeks.

Ayyoub Bouaddi will start just his third Premier League game at the expense of Fernandez, while Phil Foden and Nico O'Reilly have been brought in for Cherki and Gvardiol respectively.

While Matheus Nunes missed out through injury, Abdukodir Khusanov has shaken off a knock to start at right-back, joining O'Reilly, Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias in a four-man defence protecting goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Bouaddi will links arms with Elliot Anderson in centre-midfield, with Foden set to operate in the number 10 role between wingers Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku.

Leading the line is goal machine Erling Haaland, who has scored eight goals in as many games against Fulham and is looking to net his 10th Premier League goal of the campaign this afternoon.

As for Fulham, head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has also made a total of three changes to the team that rescued a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United a fortnight ago.

The headline alteration see Gonzalo Garcia begin as a substitute for the first time since joining the Cottagers in the summer following a run of nine straight starts without a goal.

Rodrigo Muniz, who scored a late equaliser off the bench against Newcastle, has been rewarded with his first league start of the campaign at Garcia’s expense.

Sources indicate that arbeloa has also opted to change his full-backs, with Kenny Tete and Ryan Sessegnon coming in for Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson. Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber retain their places at centre-back, though.

Man City academy graduates Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb both start against their former club, with the former to play alongside Sander Berge in midfield and the latter continuing on the right flank.

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Ndiaye, Foden, Doku; Haaland.

It has been revealed that subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, F. Samba, Lewis.

Fulham starting lineup: Leno; Tete, Affengruber, Bassey, Sessegnon; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Muniz.

Subs: Kaiser, Castagne, Cuenca, Robinson, Larsson, Cairney, Angel, Palacios, Garcia.

Breaking: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Attacking efficiency key for Hull’s visit

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (782 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that arsenal are in Premier League action this afternoon, taking on Hull City at home.
  • According to recent reports, I wrote yesterday about Viktor Gyokeres and whether his good performance in midweek would see him keep his place.
  • Industry observers note that I think everybody was so happy to see, not only the goals but also the performance, how free he looked, how happy he looked, the energy that he could transmit on that football pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that arsenal are in Premier League action this afternoon, taking on Hull City at home. No doubt there will be some rotation from the midweek Champions League game, with players like Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes, Myles-Lewis-Skelly, Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all potential inclusions. I suspect Declan Rice will start!

According to recent reports, I wrote yesterday about Viktor Gyokeres and whether his good performance in midweek would see him keep his place. On the Swedish international, Mikel Arteta said:.

Industry observers note that I think everybody was so happy to see, not only the goals but also the performance, how free he looked, how happy he looked, the energy that he could transmit on that football pitch. That’s exactly what we need, that’s what we’re signing, that’s the type of player that can help us to make the difference and he certainly did that during the night.

So let’s see if that means he keeps his place up front. Noni Madueke has had a decent couple of weeks too, with the manager revealing he’d used the elongated Interlull in October to up the ante in terms of his own training:.

What he did is he went abroad and he trained. He got somebody to train him and he went into a programme, he wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset – he wants to get better. I love that action that he took because at that moment he wasn’t playing.

In a recent development, with Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended until after the Newcastle game, he’s more or less the only option on the right-hand side, so fingers crossed he can continue that form today against a team who are likely to try and make life difficult for us. Players who can beat a man and find some space are really valuable for fixtures like this, and he might prove very important later on.

Hull started the season brightly, but haven’t won since the end of August. All the same, five draws from their last seven games tells you they’re a relatively tough nut to crack, and with a back five they’ll surely have looked at how other teams have come to our place to frustrate us. An early goal is always useful, Ezri Konsa’s quick strike against Everton probably prevented that game from being as much of a slog as it might have been, but we might also need some patience today too.

Some of the difficult games they’ve come through and competed in, they’ve earned the right to be here and been impressive. We’ve been discussing that with the boys on what to expect from them tomorrow and to be clear on what we need to do to beat them.

Arsenal were a bit wasteful in midweek against Slavia Prague, and so making the most of our chances will be important today. Whether it’s Gyokeres or Havertz, and regardless of the construction of the midfield, we need to be more clinical as a team in general, so let’s hope we can produce that today. I take nothing for granted in this league, but hopefully this is one we can just deal with as efficiently as possible before we head into the Interlull.

In a recent development, I just want to mention the launch of The 22 we had at Substantial Red last night, a huge thanks to everyone who came along and bought a book. The reaction to it was fantastic, and it was real pleasure to meet so many of you. A massive thanks too to Martin and Louise and all the staff there who were such a great help – with the Tollington closed for a while, Big Red is open today if you’re looking for your pre-game pints.

The last batch of books will go on general sale today at 6pm (UK time) via this link (which will be live at that time): https://www.yumastudios.com/store/p/the-22.

Orders are limited to two per person, and once they sell out, that’s it. This is a real collector’s item, and the best of luck if you’re after one.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool latest matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

Hopefully catch some of you a bit later on!

Breaking: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (369 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it mentioned in its October economic review.
  • The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.
  • India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it mentioned in its October economic review.

The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.

India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

The report contrasted these figures with global growth predictions of nearer 3%, saying "India's growth momentum, by comparison, has held firm.".

The ministry said growth in various key indicators like energy consumption, port traffic, goods and services tax (GST) collections, and car sales had accelerated in the previous quarter.

However, the ministry also warned of continued inflationary pressure and pressure on the rupee currency, as well as downside risks from the El Nino weather phonemenon that could threaten soil moisture ahead of the winter sowing season.

It said that external factors like oil prices and "global uncertainties" — seemingly a reference at least in part to the instablity in the Middle East — continued to pressure the rupee's value and pose inflationary risks.

Consumer price inflation (CPI), the wholesale price index (WPI), food cost prices and fuel and power prices were all rising month for month, albeit at very different rates.

The CPI was up 5.54% year-on-year in September, but the WPI had risen more sharply at 11.39%. Food index inflation was up by 8% in rural areas, and a slightly more modest 7.18% in urban centers.

But, as in many other countries, fuel and power costs increases were in an entirely different league, at 25.85% inflation in September 2026 comapred to the same month a year earlier, prior to the outbreak of fighting in the Middle East.

Recent findings suggest that although it has been a comparatively slow decline, the rupee has been consistently losing value against the US dollar over the past five years, threatening the country's relative purchasing power internationally. This slide has picked up pace in the last 15 months or so.

But the ministry pointed to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion and stated that India was "well-positioned" to weather such risks and sustain its expansionary trajectory..

  • Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.
  • Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

In a recent development, adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' remarked the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

Industry observers note that 'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards.

The fresh shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week.

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil.

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'.

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, liverpool are at the moment weighing up their options for the 2027 transfer windows.
  • Industry observers note that right now, though, it isn't.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that liverpool have had major transfer news dropped in public. We'll have to see where they go from here.

According to recent reports, liverpool are at the moment weighing up their options for the 2027 transfer windows. January feels like an important one, too, as this squad is incredibly close to being very competitive.

Industry observers note that right now, though, it isn't. Liverpool are good without being great and lack the kind of consistency that elite teams need. Keep within touching distance ahead of the transfer window, though, and the right signings could put them in the middle of the battles for silverware.

Sources indicate that there are a few areas where a signing would make a major difference. Midfield is certainly one, while there's a debate to be had about an imbalanced attack that might just benefit from an extra element.

Industry observers note that above all, there are the full-back roles. Liverpool seem unhappy about both flanks, with Andoni Iraola struggling to settle on preferred options.

It has been revealed that alejandro Balde won't be comingIt seems that one option Liverpool won't have at left-back is Barcelona's Alejandro Balde. They've been linked with the player in a relatively big way. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has reportedly spoken with the Reds about a potential move. Balde isn't playing regularly for Barcelona and looks like a clear candidate for a move this summer - and that has many teams interested. Balde is still only 23 and has the kind of experience that top clubs would love to add. It has been revealed that owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

Recent findings suggest that in short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

According to recent reports, “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche stated upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Sources indicate that krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

Breaking: Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points.
  • Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play.
  • In a recent development, and then there was Kai Havertz.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

In a recent development, and then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref remarked it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

So Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most vital thing.

It has been revealed that right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

Sources indicate that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

In a recent development, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his fresh Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Industry observers note that lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Industry observers note that arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night.
  • It has been revealed that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career.
  • Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

It has been revealed that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:.

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

According to recent reports, I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a new enough development to be fair.

I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

It has been revealed that right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.

Interlull musings and shiny distractions

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on.
  • It has been revealed that this time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally.
  • Any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

It has been revealed that this time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

Any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

According to recent reports, bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re presently 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the major guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding newly introduced frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

If you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

Given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

It has been revealed that back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

Sources indicate that with England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

Elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

It has been revealed that in other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

Sources indicate that either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023….

Myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

In a recent development, cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

In a recent development, as you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

In a recent development, on an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉.

Right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.

Jude Bellingham was one of those players.

At 16-years-old, he was already a regular for Birmingham City. As a teenager, he conquered Borussia Dortmund. And when Liverpool wanted to bring in a midfielder, the Reds were close to luring him to Anfield.

But the cajoling calls of Real Madrid are impossible to turn down. Bellingham was swayed by the allure of becoming a Galactico.

Zubimendi addresses tiredness and transfer talk
